ui.title: o pana e sike lon supa
ui.instructions: Put the ball on the table. The mechanism releases two number glyphs.

ui.title: Maze return code
ui.instructions: The three maze markers give the order. Build marker 1 → 3 → 2.

ui.title: First numeric cartouche
ui.instructions: Construct the abbreviated nanpa-format cartouche for the digit sequence 123. The nanpa glyph is reusable.

ui.title: Power sequence
ui.instructions: Reverse the five digit glyphs you learned: 5 → 4 → 3 → 2 → 1.

ui.title: Sealed numeric chamber
ui.instructions: Construct the abbreviated nanpa-format cartouche for −4.5.

ui.title: Level 1 terminal
ui.instructions: Optional archive terminal. Level progression no longer depends on confirming it.

ui.title: Missing edge digits
ui.instructions: Place the five Level 1 digit glyphs in ascending order. The machine reveals the two edge digits.

ui.title: ma seme?
ui.instructions: Identify the country, then spell its Toki Pona name using any owned glyph whose word begins with each required letter.

payload.clueTp: ma ni li lon poka suno weka Apika. ona li jo e poka telo suli.
payload.clueEn: This country is in western Africa. It has a coast on a large body of water.

ui.title: Archive sequence
ui.instructions: Use the clue 0 → 1 → 2 → 6 to build the four-glyph sequence.

ui.title: Stone index
ui.instructions: The placards read MA, then the odd positions 1, 2, 4. Enter that sequence to release the stone key.

ui.title: Coordinate map
ui.instructions: Mark the grid cell shown by the abbreviated ma coordinate.
ui.objective: Solve the coordinate map in Cartography.

ui.title: Revealed cache
ui.instructions: The cache displays three sitelen pona glyphs. Enter the same glyphs below in the same order.
ui.objective: Return to the Lower Archive and inspect the revealed cache.

ui.title: Thousands grouping
ui.instructions: Arrange 1, 2, 3, 4 in order. The grouping mechanism reveals the thousands marker.

ui.title: Notation laboratory
ui.instructions: Build the abbreviated numeric shell shown by the lab clue: 1.53. The solved apparatus reveals the scientific marker.

ui.title: Full-form bridge
ui.instructions: The full-form diagram labels four surviving positions E → EN → E → NANPA. Reconstruct them.

ui.title: Foundation complete
ui.instructions: Optional foundation terminal. The level is already complete once all required glyphs and mandatory world-state objectives are satisfied.

ui.title: Clock alignment
ui.instructions: Set the three clock dials so all three clues are true. This is a deduction puzzle; the dials can be changed independently.

ui.title: Relay routing
ui.instructions: Rotate the relay pieces to make one continuous signal path from the left input to the right output.

ui.title: Beacon route
ui.instructions: Move the marker through checkpoints A, B, C in that order, then reach the exit. Dark cells are blocked.

ui.title: Observation lights
ui.instructions: Make all nine lamps glow. Tapping a lamp also changes its orthogonal neighbours.

ui.title: Balance machine
ui.instructions: Select a combination of the four available weights that exactly balances the target mass. Each weight can be used once.

ui.title: Synchronization core
ui.instructions: The wall display is explicitly a time: 03:09. Choose the rendered cartouche that belongs on the time circuit.

foundationMilestone.note: By the end of Level 2 the guaranteed inventory covers every Toki Pona initial and the collectible repertoire needed for ordinary abbreviated decimal nanpa-linja-n cartouches. kin and kipisi are baseline.
